items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1960-01-03
items.q: He played ragtime drums, and he asked me if I'd take a job in his band.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. Oh, and this is the famous Papa Lane you used to call him.
That's right, old man Lane. He played ragtime drums, and he asked me if I'd take a job in his band.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: And I had this man, La Rocca, in the band.

ctx.x: And I'll tell you, it was one night. How I come not to go up there, it was another political parade I was playing. And I had this man, La Rocca, in the band. Nick La Rocca? He played with me, too. I'd pick up La Rocca when he hardly heard anything about it, Trumper. And I'm playing the music on the street. Some fellas stepped in and was told to me after.
I'll ask Paul. I'll ask Paul.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: But when I'd take him in the parades, I'd pay him as well as I paid the rest of the men.

ctx.x: He said he did? Yes, there was a magazine article in the paper about that. And I will be willing. I'd go stand up anyways. I'd fight him to the last. Because he is a liar. Plain-faced liar. He didn't even know how to put the connet in his mouth at that time. When he first started to play, when he used to be at Elmire Pleasure Ground with him. And after that, he used to come to the house there on Charter Street and try to rehearse them. Manuel tried to show him how to play. Then after that, he used to leave them…

Of course, he began to improve a considerable lot. Yeah. But when I'd take him in the parades, I'd pay him as well as I paid the rest of the men. So he couldn't play much then? Well, he couldn't play very much, no. In fact, whether he didn't know how to play these numbers or not, I don't know. But eventually he did. He got onto all of that stuff, you see. Then he began to play the connet pretty good. He played a pretty good trumpet.

That's another liar. That he... That Tiger Rag. He's another liar. He didn't write Tiger Rag. No, he didn't. No, not half of it, no. Because he played... And Alcide Nunes, they used to call it plurine and meatballs, the same thing. And he's the one that played it, but not La Raffin.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: And the first thing you know, I got through that much work, Johnny, that I put him in the band anyhow to fill out.

ctx.x: All right, he said. If you say so, it's all right. We stood by number nine, Jane Jane House, on Decatur and Espinade. I lined them all around the circle. Said to the Chinaman, I said, whenever you can catch time, the Chinaman, that you can fill up a note, put it in there. This baritone, I said, hold up as much as possible for you. All right. Put the tuba in the Chinaman's hand. Every night we played for two weeks. Every night for two weeks. Chinaman on the tube. Start to put them in parades. Start to moat around.…
